changes.from:
Write docs/adr/0004-look-identity-recipes.md, spec/look.md and spec/look.schema.json.

Content to decide and record:
- Look = id, name, version, pinned scheme pair (dark + light ids), identity, recipes. Colour-only schemes (e.g. Nord) combine only with the Oqto Look in v1, to keep the test matrix small.
- Identity: sans/mono/display font as a web fallback stack plus a single GPUI family name; unsupported fonts fail closed to the Oqto Look. Radius dial unchanged. Validate radius against control height so compact controls never turn into pills by accident.
- control recipe (first and only recipe in v1):
  - elevation: flat | hairline | raised(sm | md). Exactly one mechanism, so border + shadow on one element is unrepresentable. Hover is derived (raised lifts one step, flat/hairline tint), not a free value.
  - hairline colour: a role reference plus an integer alpha (border and surface bind the same slot, so the plain border role is invisible on cards). No new portable roles.
  - border width 0 | 1, derived from elevation.
  - density: compact | regular | comfortable, named per-surface tables of integer px (height, horizontal padding, gap). A Look may pin explicit numbers when no table fits (the Oqto Look will).
  - focus: ring | outline | tint | indicator, with width and offset where meaningful. "none" is not a value. Every value must give at least 3:1 focused-vs-unfocused difference against each adjacent surface in both modes.
  - shadows as structured layers (y, blur, spread, integer alpha, colour role), never CSS strings, so GPUI can build BoxShadow from the same data.
- Web-only effects (backdrop blur, glass) stay out of the v1 cross-surface contract.
- Indicators (active tab underline, thinking bar) are a later separate recipe, radius-aware; not part of control.
- ring stays expressible; house Looks do not use it (user preference).

Update spec/effects.md to point at the ADR. Numbers must be integers or exact binary fractions (cross-language parity risk seen when porting to Rust f32).

Proof: schema validates the Lumen and Moss control recipes exported by ~/byteowlz/design-studio and rejects focus "none", border+shadow combinations and unknown enum values (add fixtures for each). Keep repo checks green.
